claims.explanation: Latrepirdine's selective killing of cancer cell lines is most strongly associated with the presence of TP53 mutations, which are enriched in sensitive lines and may impair DNA damage responses or autophagy, enhancing cytotoxicity. Additionally, mutations in DNA damage response genes (ATM, SF3B1) and activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway (via PTEN loss or PIK3CA mutation) appear to sensitize cells, possibly by disrupting autophagy regulation. Conversely, KRAS mutations are enriched in resistant lines, suggesting that KRAS-driven oncogenic signaling may protect against latrepirdine-induced cell death.
